A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same study, including their appendices, equations, figures, and tables. Changed models and experimental settings prevent direct performance comparisons but support a reliable assessment of the revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark accuracies, activation-patching experiments, vocabulary projections, attention-component analyses, and training-checkpoint results.

after.justification: V2 reports original four-choice benchmark results, mechanistic interventions, symbol-format and zero-shot analyses, and training-checkpoint measurements.

M1.justification: The underlying procedures remain activation patching and vocabulary projection at layer, function, and attention-head levels. V2 changes the studied models, task settings, and diagnostic scores without introducing a new model architecture or fundamentally different analysis algorithm.

E1.justification: HellaSwag, MMLU, and Colors remain, but their binary formulations become four-choice tasks. V1's A/B and C/D scenarios are replaced by A/B/C/D, random letters Q/Z/R/X and O/E/B/P, and numeric symbols 1/2/3/4. These substantially change answer-selection requirements and tested symbol environments.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed solver or interpretability algorithm against a competing baseline suite. Activation patching and vocabulary projection remain complementary tools; the replaced language models are subjects of analysis.

E3.justification: Llama2 and earlier Olmo models are replaced by Llama3.1, Olmo0724, and Qwen2.5. V2 adds zero-shot settings and logit-based measurements. General HellaSwag/MMLU samples change from 5,000 to 1,000; patching already used 1,000 in v1. The stated HellaSwag split changes from validation to test. Prompt averaging, example selection, and checkpoint sampling also change. Checkpoint projections switch from all instances in v1 Figure 22 to correctly predicted instances in v2 Figure 27.

E4.justification: V2 adds zero-versus-three-shot mechanistic comparisons, broader symbol-format robustness analyses, explicit individual-head causal interventions (Figure 13), and finer training-trajectory analyses. It removes v1's generative-versus-MCQA projection comparison, correctness-conditioned analyses (Figures 11–13), and detailed consistency breakdowns (Tables 4–5).

E5.justification: V2's reproducibility statement newly reports that random seeds were fixed. It supplies neither seed values nor repeated-run counts, so this is additional reporting rather than evidence of increased replication. No new uncertainty-estimation or significance-testing procedure is specified.

E6.justification: Most results are replaced under new models and four-choice settings. V1 identifies layer 21 for Olmo-SFT and brackets Olmo-v1.7 learning between 350B and 1T tokens; v2 identifies layer 24 for Olmo0724 Instruct and an 80k–100k-step learning transition for Olmo0724 Base. V2 Figure 27 reports checkpoint accuracies of 25%, 97%, 81%, and 100%. These are newly reported results under different conditions, not matched performance improvements.

T1.justification: V2 Section 4.3 adds the no-output-layer-normalization condition for interpreting logit contributions as additive and loosely causal; Footnote 10 states the component-wise additive logit property. The Transformer derivations in Equations (1)–(3) remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central selection, promotion, and symbol-alignment account remains. The abstract changes causal localization from a single middle layer to a few layers and replaces its categorical poor-model separability statement with continued growth of logit differences during training. The introduction also qualifies cross-task similarity as applying when predictions are correct.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes accurate answer ranking from large probability margins, interprets effects of in-context examples, and proposes separate positional and symbol-encoding roles for different layers. It further distinguishes MLP-wide logit increases from discriminative attention contributions. Core methodological limitations move to Appendix B, while v1's explicit model-generality caveat and suggested incorrect-prediction comparison are omitted.

D1.justification: V2 adds a reproducibility statement and an explicit public location for the Colors dataset while retaining the existing code link. It also documents example-position selection and checkpoint steps for the revised experiments. No substantial new hardware or runtime information is provided.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting logit-based analysis and mechanistic terminology, including Zhang and Nanda, Saphra and Wiegreffe, and Zhu et al., alongside new model references. Its comparison with Lieberum et al. emphasizes training behavior and synthetic-task coverage more strongly, while the overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: The experimental and interpretive narrative is substantially rewritten. V2 separates task notation, adds a Logits vs. Probits subsection, restructures the component-analysis discussion, relocates most limitations to Appendix B, and adds a reproducibility statement. The broad eight-section outline remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column conference formatting. Many plots are redesigned with paired logit/probability panels, additional token traces, and revised legends. Component bar charts give way to heatmaps, checkpoint bars become trajectories, and v1's five tables disappear. The overview and Transformer diagrams are substantially retained.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central mechanistic account: four-choice tests address v1's binary-task restriction, while complementary logit measurements and explicit head-level interventions provide more discriminating evidence for the proposed mechanisms. Symbol-format and zero-shot analyses better establish their boundaries. Smaller samples and removed correctness/consistency breakdowns sacrifice useful detail, but the stronger causal evidence and more nuanced distinction between accuracy and token margins provide a clear overall gain.
